minutes.headline: Task force debated funding storm water via a new utility fee vs. a tax override, sparring over overhead
minutes.summary: The Stormwater Task Force reviewed new GIS impervious-area data for roughly 700 properties to build a utility fee model, then spent most of the meeting arguing over how much administrative overhead a stand-alone stormwater utility would carry compared with keeping the work in the town's operating budget. No formal decision was reached on funding approach; the group agreed to build a side-by-side cost comparison for a future presentation and to nail down the next meeting date.

budget_items.topic: Lunenburg Crossing stormwater fee vs. tax bill
budget_items.what_was_said: The group discussed that a large commercial property's tax bill was much larger than its estimated stormwater utility fee would be, estimating the fee at roughly 15% of that tax bill as a comparison point.

budget_items.topic: Junior engineer position and utility overhead
budget_items.what_was_said: Members discussed that if a proposed junior engineer position is funded in the town's override budget, its salary would be removed from the storm water utility's overhead calculation.
The group discussed a roughly 30% overhead figure on Bill's stormwater budget, questioning what indirect costs (accounting, treasury, legal) made up that share.
A member walked through a spreadsheet formula summing indirect cost lines to produce the overhead total being debated.

budget_items.topic: Full stormwater funding in override budget
budget_items.what_was_said: It was noted that full funding of storm water almost made it into a tier-one override budget this year but did not, which a member called a disappointment.

budget_items.topic: Cap on fee relative to assessed value
budget_items.what_was_said: A member suggested flagging or capping the stormwater fee for small businesses if it exceeded some threshold share of their assessed property value.

budget_items.topic: Residential vs. business share of cost under utility vs. tax funding
budget_items.what_was_said: A member estimated that under a utility approach residents would bear a much smaller share of storm water cost than under the current property-tax-funded approach.

decisions.decision: One member will enter the new impervious-area data into the broader fee spreadsheet and calculate a proposed fee for each property using the task force's current tier structure.
The group agreed to build the overhead comparison as three columns: operating-budget cost, utility cost, and the difference (net overhead) between them, for the next presentation.
The task force agreed its next public/Finance Committee presentation should center on the financial impact and cost comparison to residents, rather than general storm water education.
The task force set its next meeting for May 14th.

what_happened.line: No decision was made on funding stormwater through a new utility fee versus the town's tax-funded operating budget, after debate over utility overhead.
The group agreed to build a comparison of operating-budget cost, utility cost, and the difference between them for a future presentation.
That presentation will focus on the financial impact and cost comparison to residents, not general stormwater education.
A property-fee model is being built from GIS impervious-surface data for roughly 700 properties, with a fee to be calculated for each.
The next meeting is set for May 14.

why_it_matters: This decides whether stormwater work shows up as a new separate fee on a resident's bill or stays folded into the property tax rate.
How overhead and cost are split between a stand-alone utility and the operating budget could shift how much of the cost businesses versus homeowners pay.
No funding method has been chosen yet; the task force is still building the cost comparison that would inform that choice.
